Marginal likelihood of a drmTMB model with priors

Source: R/marglik.R
marglik.Rd

The log marginal likelihood log p(y), the likelihood integrated over the prior of all parameters, for Bayesian model comparison and model averaging: the posterior probability of a model is proportional to its prior probability times its marginal likelihood.

Usage

marglik(object, method = c("laplace", "is"), n = 5000, df = 4)

Arguments

object

a drmTMB object, fitted with priors for all parameters

method

"laplace" (default) or "is" (importance sampling)

n

number of draws of the final round of importance sampling

df

degrees of freedom of the multivariate t proposal of importance sampling

Value

the log marginal likelihood, a number of class "drcmarglik" with the attributes method, the number of parameters k, and for importance sampling n, the effective sample size ess, the Monte Carlo standard error se, the number of draws whose objective could not be evaluated (failed, given weight 0), and the Laplace approximation laplace.

Details

The fit needs a proper prior for every estimated parameter (see priors): all free coefficients, the standard deviations of the random effects, the residual parameter (sigma, phi or theta) and the parameters of a residual correlation structure or variance function (see correlation); with a flat prior, the marginal likelihood is not defined. Correlations of random effects have no priors, so that random effects of several parameters or with slopes need independent terms (|| or separate formulas). The random effects are integrated out by the Laplace approximation of the fit.

method="laplace" approximates the log posterior of the parameters (on the scale of their optimisation, with the log Jacobians of the priors) by a normal distribution at the posterior mode: log p(y) = -objective + k/2 log(2 pi) - 1/2 log det H, with k parameters and the Hessian H of the objective, as in the Bayesian benchmark dose modelling of EFSA (2022). The random effects are integrated out first, so that this is a nested Laplace approximation. It is poor if the posterior mode is close to a bound, e.g. of a pert prior or a multistage coefficient at 0, which gives a warning. For small dose-response data sets, the Laplace approximation can be noticeably biased, in particular with posterior modes close to the bounds of pert priors, which changes the posterior model probabilities by a few percentage points; check it with method="is".

method="is" estimates the marginal likelihood by adaptive importance sampling. The proposal is a multivariate t distribution with df degrees of freedom, first centred at the posterior mode with the covariance of the fit as its scale matrix; three rounds of n/2 draws (at least 10 per parameter) move it to the weighted mean and covariance of the draws, which follows skewed or curved posteriors (e.g. a strong correlation of the log BMD with the slope), and a final round of n draws gives the estimate. The proposal of each round is a mixture, with probability 0.2 of the initial proposal, so that the weights stay bounded in its tails. Draws outside the bounds of the parameters have weight 0. The result reports the effective sample size of the weights of the final round and the Monte Carlo standard error of the log marginal likelihood; a small effective sample size (e.g. below 100) means the estimate is unreliable. With random effects, each draw needs an inner optimisation, so that importance sampling is slower.

See also

bmdbayes, priors, bmdefsa

Examples

# proper priors for all estimated parameters, in the BMD parameterisation
pr <- list(bmd = pert(0.1, 1, 5), b2 = normal(8, 1), b3 = normal(-2, 2), sigma = half_normal(1))
fit <- function(model)
  drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = model,
         start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE),
         bmdpar = list(bmr = 0.05, def = "relative"), prior = pr)
LL <- fit("loglogistic")
W2 <- fit("weibull2")
marglik(LL)
#> Log marginal likelihood: -27.05 
#> Laplace approximation, 4 parameters
marglik(W2)
#> Log marginal likelihood: -25.77 
#> Laplace approximation, 4 parameters
# importance sampling as a check of the Laplace approximation
set.seed(1)
marglik(LL, method = "is", n = 2000)
#> Log marginal likelihood: -26.83 
#> Importance sampling, 2000 draws, effective sample size 1174
#> Monte Carlo standard error 0.019; Laplace approximation -27.05
